recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core-source follow-up is recommended for FHIR-19455; future accession-number changes should be handled through the later ImagingStudy accession issue family.
issue_request: FHIR-19455 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for STU3 and asked for additional ImagingStudy guidance and examples for DICOM Study, Series, and SOP Instance UID encoding, including system urn:dicom:uid and value prefix urn:oid: when a DICOM UID is represented as an Identifier, plus an ACSN accession-number example.
initial_application: The Jira comment records application on branch moehrke_ii_uid. Git history does not show a commit subject explicitly naming FHIR-19455, but merge 5ccbf09b4f brought in commit 131af0770a from that branch, which updated ImagingStudy notes and examples in the same UID/change family as FHIR-19455, FHIR-19456, and FHIR-18064.
additional_context: ImagingStudy is active in source/fhir.ini. Later applied/published ImagingStudy issues refined the accession-number part of the original guidance: FHIR-22118 moved accession away from ImagingStudy.identifier to basedOn.identifier, FHIR-49675 restored that model after a brief R6 reversal, FHIR-46224 kept the UID/accession note anchors linkable, and FHIR-56033 removed remaining accession-number wording from ImagingStudy.identifier comments.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. No source change is needed because the current ImagingStudy notes state the requested DICOM UID encoding, the examples show the requested system/value patterns, and the current accession text intentionally follows later basedOn.identifier guidance rather than the older FHIR-19455 accession snippet.

related_jiras.note: The same moehrke_ii_uid application reverted series and instance identifiers to uid/id values, which is part of the UID encoding context.
The same application family addressed distinguishing DICOM UID identifiers and influenced the current ImagingStudy.identifier guidance.
Later Published decision separated accession number from ImagingStudy.identifier and placed it on basedOn.identifier.
Later Applied issue briefly moved accession number to ImagingStudy.identifier before FHIR-49675 reversed that direction.
Later Applied decision made the DICOM UID and Accession Number notes referenceable from detailed descriptions without changing the UID rule.
Later Applied decision restored the accession-number basedOn.identifier model; it is already represented on the combined branch.
Later Applied decision removed remaining accession-number wording from ImagingStudy.identifier comments.
